clue.text: Sort of stop exchanging rook for bishop: what's left for you?

indicators.note: exchanging one thing for another swaps a letter out and puts a different one in its place

parts.note: a request stop is a bus stop where the bus halts only if asked
R is the chess notation for rook
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A chess player muses about swapping pieces in some kind of blockade, then asks what remains.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the R of REQUEST for B to get BEQUEST. The chess pieces suggest a game, but they only supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is property left to someone in a will, so it is what's left for you.

clue.text: What are essential pens like being gripped?

indicators.note: something being gripped is held inside whatever holds it

parts.note: Bics are ballpoint pens, from the brand name
as means like, in a comparison

explanation.surface: A question asking which pens are indispensable when they are being held.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bic is a cheap ballpoint pen; the brand name is used for any such pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The basics are the fundamental, indispensable things you cannot do without.

clue.text: One of several children holds a tango old-fashioned

indicators.note: a thing that holds another keeps it within its own walls

parts.note: a quin is one of five children born at one birth
taken as written
Tango is T in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A quintuplet clutching a tango record that is out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIN holds A, giving QU(A)IN, then T is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint describes something charmingly old-fashioned, attractive because of its antique character.

clue.text: Mark on score, one very obscured by coffee

indicators.note: something obscured by another is hidden inside or behind it

parts.note: espresso is strong black Italian coffee
I is the Roman numeral for one
V is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A musician complains that a marking on the sheet music is very obscured by spilt coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'obscured' sound like a stain; here it just means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Espressivo is an Italian direction written on sheet music telling the player to perform expressively.

clue.text: Changes course, not a time for assaults

indicators.note: not means the named letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: attacks are assaults
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A general's strategy shifts direction, avoiding a moment to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and T from the front of ATTACKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing boat tacks when it turns into the wind to change its heading.

clue.text: Being on duty, stop light reflecting through airport

indicators.note: something running through another passes inside it

parts.note: Orly is a Paris airport

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: the red traffic light means stop

explanation.surface: Someone on duty at an airport sees a red signal reflecting off the glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun here, a person, not part of a verb phrase. Orly is one of the two main Paris airports.
explanation.definitionFit: An orderly is an attendant, in a hospital or the army, who is a person on duty to carry out tasks.

clue.text: Petition the family's obese woman

parts.note: a family speaking of what belongs to them says our
obese means fat
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A household lodges a complaint about a heavy woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a prayer, the Lord's Prayer, which opens with these two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Father, the Lord's Prayer, is a petition to God, a set of requests for bread and forgiveness.

clue.text: Act certainly in this

parts.note: surface reading: someone is told to act decisively in this matter
setter's reading: the word for certainly can be split as 'in' plus this act, so this is the act that certainly sits in

explanation.surface: An instruction to behave with conviction in a given situation.
explanation.walkthrough: INDEED means certainly; split it as IN plus the answer and it literally reads 'in this'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is an act or action, something done, as in good deeds.

clue.text: Soldiers doing parachuting, a bit of a shower

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
in, as in taking part, engaged in something
a drop is a parachute descent

explanation.surface: Troops on a parachute exercise, part of a shower of descending soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a shower of paratroopers; the definition means a rain shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A raindrop is a single drop of water, one small part of a rain shower.

clue.text: Married before, after a month was up daughter sounded off loudly

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: May is a month
M is the abbreviation for married
ere is an old word for before
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A wedding story told after a month: a daughter made a loud fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a month' places the married-before letters behind the upturned month, so the month leads the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to complain or talk loudly and persistently, to sound off.

clue.text: Millions offered in exchange are overwhelming

definitions.note: plural verb phrase; 'they swamp' means 'they are overwhelming'

indicators.note: something offered in another is placed within it

parts.note: a swap is an exchange
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: Huge sums put up in a trade deal are too much to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a plural verb phrase: 'they swamp' is 'they are overwhelming'.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp is to overwhelm, flood with too much, as water floods a boat.

clue.text: Long to have maiden on rug shortly? Seize the chance!

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a carpet is a floor rug
to be dying for something is to long for it
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to have a young woman on the rug, and urges taking the opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places DIE and M after the shortened rug. A maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpe diem is Latin for 'seize the day', a call to make the most of the moment.

clue.text: Study arousing the body by mutual agreement

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
sensual means gratifying the bodily senses

explanation.surface: A study of sexual arousal conducted with everyone's agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for study is an old verb, as in conning one's lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Consensual means done with the consent of all involved, which is mutual agreement.

clue.text: Paid less, content to be shirking

indicators.note: the content of something is what sits inside it, so the answer is held within the words

parts.note: the inner letters of these two words run together

explanation.surface: A worker on lower wages is happy to slack off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy', but it means the inside of the preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being idle is avoiding work, which is what shirking means.

clue.text: Killer I sidetrack, caught leaving plant

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, Cleopatra's killer
taken as written
to sidetrack someone is to distract them
ct is a scorecard abbreviation for caught in cricket

explanation.surface: A murderer confesses to diverting attention, and was caught before running off.
explanation.walkthrough: Take CT off the end of DISTRACT. The aspidistra is a hardy houseplant famous in Victorian parlours.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a leafy plant, a classic indoor pot plant.

clue.text: Sounder of body? Keep it firm with pressure, squeezed into tights

indicators.note: something squeezed into another is pushed inside it

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand
hose is an old word for tights or stockings
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping something firm with pressure by squeezing it into tights, as if a body-shaping tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounder' means a thing that sounds, that is, listens to the body. Stet is the proofreader's instruction to restore a deleted word.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's stethoscope is used to sound, or listen to, the chest and other parts of the body.

clue.text: One to take to bed, I wondered idly?

indicators.note: doing something idly is doing it aimlessly, so the letters are jumbled carelessly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone muses idly about which thing to bring to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is a playful one.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt filled with down, something you take to bed to keep warm.

clue.text: Small letter, more yellowy

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a letter can be one who lets, that is allows

explanation.surface: A tiny written character described as more yellow in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is not an alphabet character but one who lets things happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallow describes a sickly yellowish complexion, so sallower is more yellowish.

clue.text: Cricketing medic accepting a test of acceleration

indicators.note: someone accepting a thing takes it in among them

parts.note: Dr W.G. Grace was the great Victorian cricketer, a qualified doctor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketing doctor agrees to a trial of speed.
explanation.walkthrough: W.G. Grace, a qualified doctor, was England's most famous Victorian cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag race is a short sprint between cars from a standing start, testing how fast they accelerate.

clue.text: Appear to have cried piteously for so long

parts.note: to arrive is to appear on the scene

indicators.note: something done piteously is done in a wretched, broken state, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone turns up having wept miserably for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a stretch of time, but it is the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrivederci is Italian for goodbye, the same farewell as 'so long'.

clue.text: Oriental sort of bean these days unknown to British Isles

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
Z is an algebraic unknown
the UK is Britain
I is the abbreviation for island or isle

explanation.surface: A type of Asian bean that is now unfamiliar in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the bean is unknown here; 'unknown' is just the letter of algebra.
explanation.definitionFit: The adzuki is a small red bean grown in East Asia, used in Japanese sweet bean paste.

clue.text: In the cold, abandon trade fair, having seen half

indicators.note: having half means only part survives, the rest of the word being dropped

parts.note: an expo is an exhibition or trade fair
taken as written

explanation.surface: Leaving a trade show out in the cold after seeing only half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the first half of SEEN. To expose a baby was to abandon it outdoors to the elements.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose someone is to leave them unprotected from the weather, abandoned out in the cold.

clue.text: Eleven? You have two

definitions.meaning: first meaning: '... eleven' is the bingo call for 11, whose two strokes look like a pair of ...
second meaning: what a person has two of, the limbs they walk on

explanation.walkthrough: Bingo callers have rhyming or pictorial names for numbers; 11 is 'legs eleven'.
explanation.definitionFit: Legs are the limbs people stand on, and the digits 11 resemble a pair of them.

clue.text: Considers turbulent times a pointer

indicators.note: turbulent means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on troubled times and seeks a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent times' looks like a phrase, but only 'turbulent' works on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-index is a reference directing the reader to another entry, a pointer within an index.

clue.text: Fight over old earth

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the later-named piece sits on top of the earlier one

parts.note: a sett is a badger's earth, or burrow
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A dispute over ancient land.
explanation.walkthrough: A badger's home is called a sett or an earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a fight or a heated argument, a brief bout of conflict.

clue.text: I agree, German police not content it's a prank

indicators.note: without its content the word keeps only its outside, its middle being emptied out

parts.note: ja is German for yes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that a trick played on German officers was a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep only the outside letters of POLICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a practical joke or prank, a piece of mischief.

clue.text: Wasn't that a great fight! Have you forgotten?

definitions.note: an exclamation, read with the answer split as 'What a bout!'
definitions.meaning: first meaning: split differently, the phrase is an exclamation praising a boxing match, a bout being a fight
second meaning: a prompt reminding someone of a thing they have overlooked

explanation.walkthrough: Move the space one letter to the left and the phrase becomes a cry of admiration at a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking 'what about X?' reminds a listener of something they have overlooked or neglected.

clue.text: Cathedral men returning to follow the faith? No way

indicators.note: to follow places one piece after another in the finished word
no way means the abbreviation for a road or street is removed

parts.note: trust is faith
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A cathedral's congregation of men coming back to the faith, with no other path.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop ST from TRUST, then add OR reversed. Truro is a cathedral city in Cornwall, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro is a city whose cathedral is its landmark, so the name stands for that cathedral.

clue.text: Dare one to blow up school

indicators.note: something blown up is shattered, so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pupil challenges another to blow up the school.
explanation.walkthrough: Roedean is a famous girls' boarding school near Brighton, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a well-known English independent school for girls.

clue.text: Glass, one taken after mate in one

indicators.note: something in another is held inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: taken after means placed behind the other piece in reading order

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A drinking glass, one taken after a friend, all in one.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'one's do different jobs: the first is a Roman numeral, the second is the word itself, which holds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline is a milky, semi-translucent glass resembling opal.
